title: Other taxi halls and visiting players jamming
summary: Band sizes shrinking, the other taxi halls, and hotel musicians who came to jam.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, I'm really surprised that I had the three saxophones. I always thought those people were real cheap and random. Taxi dance-offs. How many pieces did they usually have?
How many pieces did they usually have? What did they have?
I see they had three saxophones and three rhythm. Six. Six.

Six pieces. But then at one point they had three songs? They wound up I believe with four. Four or five were, when, when, when, when, when, when, when the taxes went down. You don't have to pay more money. They cut out people. Yeah.
Yeah. And they had the, the fern, the bud washer. Tuxedo. The tuxedo. Alamo. Alamo. Music box. Music box. That's all I know.
Five. Five. Five. Five. Five. Five.
Five. Five. Five. Five. Five. Five. Well what about the white people, did they play any of those white musicians? Did they play music then?

Well we only had musicians from the Road Power Hotel used to come and sing with us. Oh I had? Such as the big bands like maybe Ice and Jones or somebody like that. All the good musicians when they get off, you see, cause at that time we was getting off at 5 o'clock. And they'd come in and it was a good place for them to jam, you know. You call it ballet, we call it jamming. It was a good place for them to jam, they would come and jam with us.
